method: Source-backed semantic review and image inspection of each diagram's 1440x900 light and dark first-screen captures. The rule walkthrough was also inspected in full at 2048x1320.

diagrams.note: Original overview preserved byte-for-byte; the main path and optional rule branch remain clear.
Packet, conversation and host-profile branches remain distinct; enrichment inputs reach their owning producer.
Recovered content and optional File audit output are separate; analyzer failures withhold readiness.
Saved alert history is the highlighted outcome; explicit webhook delivery is a secondary branch.
Three actual runtime modes; explicit approval and prior-mode resume remain qualified by source-backed notes.
Bind, search, resolve and review phases separate the long sequence; readable vertical scrolling is intentional.
ACK after gzip flush and fsync at close are visible in the drawing; enrollment and record transport are distinct.
Four parallel identification methods; DPI classification does not imply plaintext or parser output.
Client and server claims are attributed separately; Passive WebTech does not feed host CVE enrichment.
Unresolved identity, unavailable enrichment and no confirmed applicability are distinct outcomes; writer selection is visible.
Reference metadata, optional catalogue association and observed activity remain separate; community catalogue emptiness is visible.
Synthetic records and times are explicit; group isolation, nonmatches, threshold reset and alert output are legible. Phase frames clear the notes.
Audit, inline admission, rejection and retrospective capture are separate lanes; monitor/enforce conditions remain explicit.
Three detector inputs, evidence families and coverage checks can be compared row-by-row.

pitfalls: Put behavior-changing conditions in visible labels or sublabels; optional tag metadata is not shown in every reader mode.
Reserve note clearance inside sequence phase frames, not only between message arrows.
Separate connected workflow outcomes before adding fixed route pins; fixed pins can defeat automatic placement.
